newsitem.title: USA: UAL reaches tentative wage pact with pilots.
newsitem.headline: UAL reaches tentative wage pact with pilots.

text.p: UAL Corp said on Wednesday its United Airlines operating subsidiary reached a tentative agreement with the Air Line Pilots Association (ALPA) that includes four wage increases through 2000.
Under the agreement, United pilots will receive wage increases of three percent in both 1997 and 1998 and an additional two percent in both 1999 and 2000, UAL said.
Pilots will also be eligible for lump-sum profit-sharing payments in 1998 and 1999 based on the carrier's performance in the next two years, the airline said.
ALPA members will vote on the proposal in December.

The wage negotiation was built into UAL's July 1994 original employee stock ownership plan (ESOP) agreement with the ALPA. At that time, the pilots union agreed to wage cuts and work-rule changes in exchange for a stake in the airline.
The agreement covers 8,500 United Airlines pilots and is scheduled to expire in 2000.
The International Association of Machinists and salaried employees at UAL also gained a stake in the carrier in exchange for concessions.

"United's and ALPA's negotiators worked long and hard to reach an agreement that successfully balances the interests of United stockholders, our employees and our need to keep costs competitive," UAL Chairman and Chief Executive Officer Gerald Greenwald said.
Results of the ALPA vote are expected in mid-January, UAL spokesman Tony Molinaro said.

UAL has been negotiating with both ALPA and IAM members on a wage increase since last summer. Earlier this year the Association of Flight Attendants, which did not participate in the ESOP in 1994, rejected a proposed labor agreement with UAL that did not include any wage increases in 1996.
UAL has credited concessions gained in the ESOP in part for improved profitability at the airline.

Last month it reported a sharp rise in earnings for the third quarter, the 14th consecutive three-month period in which the company reported year-over-year improvement. Its operating earnings for the third quarter of $470.0 million, or $3.58 a share, excluding charges, up from $330 million, or $2.53.
